title: I NEED MY SPACE, Mission to Mars and Exploring Wind Tunnels

pages.text: Jenna Eppink and Christie Funk NASA Langley Research Center I NEED MY SPACE Mission to Mars and Exploring Wind Tunnels

MISSION TO MARS • WHAT ARE SOME CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH A MISSION TO MARS? Trip Time –Round trip human expedition to Mars: 2-3 years (incl. time spent on the Red Planet) »Astronauts lose muscle and bone mass due to microgravity »Radiation exposure »How to provide enough supplies »How to store enough fuel

MISSION TO MARS • HOW WOULD YOU GO FROM THE EARTH TO MARS? STRAIGHT LINE? • HOW FAR ARE THE EARTH AND MARS FROM THE SUN? – The Earth is 149,600,000 km from the Sun – Mars is 227,940,000 km from the Sun – Scale for today’s activity: 1 cm = 10,000,000 km

The NASA Langley Transonic Dynamics Tunnel (TDT) Test section: 16 feet x 16 feet Test medium: R-134a or Air Mach number range: 0 to 1.2 Total pressure range: 0.01 to 1.0 atmosphere Dynamic pressure (max): 550 psf (R-134a) / 320 psf (Air) National Aeronautics and Space Administration
